newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty weakens vs basket, 1-day depos up.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty weakens vs basket, 1-day depos up.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed lower against the basket of currencies after it eased against the mark because of a difference in value dates, dealers said.
They said banks had to add the cost of carry to spot mark/zloty deals with value date December 30 against the value date for dollar/zloty on December 27.
"The mark was traded slightly higher because of additional cost of financing, but banks stopped quoting at about 11 local time and trade was very weak," said Piotr Czyzewski from ING Bank Warsaw.

The zloty closed at 3.18/3.12 percent from the parity rate, weaker than Friday's 3.31/3.19 percent. It closed at 2.8600/15 to the dollar against Friday's 2.8585/20 and at 1.8433/47 to the mark, down from 1.8380/05.

Overnight rates closed at 21.50/22.50 percent, up from opening's 21.20/21.50 percent after the central bank sold nominally 270 million zlotys of its 91-day and 182-day NBP-bills with overnight value date.
Tomorrow/next rates closed at 21.50/22.40 percent, up from opening's 21.00/22.00 percent after NBP drained 262 million zlotys for 14 days at a maximum rate of 21.64 percent.
The NBP said it would wait for December CPI data before it decides if it has to raise official rates but fast credit growth is likely to make the decision unavoidable.
Polish food prices rose 0.3 percent in the December 10-20 period after rising 1.9 percent in the previous 10 days and were 2.3 percent higher than in the November 10-20 period.

Earlier today Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko told a news conference Polish inflation should fall to about 18 percent from 21.6 percent last year. He also said the Polish economy is likely to expand in 1996 by 6.7 to 7.0 percent.
